title: Zeroth derived global sections preserves quasi-coherent coproducts
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme]. In $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], let $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ be any set-indexed family of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology, and let $\iota_i:E_i\to S$ exhibit $S$ as their ambient coproduct. Put $F(E)=H^0(R\Gamma(X,E))$ as an additive group, using the module-valued global-sections functor [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and its unbounded derived functor [def-pc-global-derived-rhom]. The homomorphism $\bigoplus_{i\in I}F(E_i)\to F(S)$ induced on the i-th summand by $F(\iota_i)$ is bijective. The assertion includes the empty family and arbitrary unbounded complexes.

proof.text: Let a:X → Spec(ULift ℤ) be the structure morphism. It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because X is qcqs and the target is affine. By [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-direct-sums], Ra_* preserves the ambient coproduct of the E_i. Its terms are quasi-coherent by [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh].

source.place: Proposition perfect-proposition-compact-is-perfect (Tag 09M1), proof, first paragraph; structure-sheaf case

proof.text: The equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] computes RΓ on Spec(ULift ℤ) by module complexes, and preserves coproducts. Global sections after Ra_* compute RΓ(X,-): underived global sections after a_* are global sections on X with scalar action restricted to ℤ, and K-injective resolutions compute both derived functors as in [def-pc-global-derived-rhom] and [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]. Thus it suffices to compute H^0 of the module coproduct.

source.place: Proposition perfect-proposition-compact-is-perfect (Tag 09M1), proof, first paragraph; structure-sheaf case

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-derived-module-direct-sums] to represent that coproduct by termwise sums. Exactness of module direct sums identifies kernels and images of the sum differential with sums of kernels and images, so H^0 of the termwise sum is the direct sum of H^0. The identifications commute with every coprojection. Forgetting ring actions preserves the resulting additive bijection. Therefore it is precisely the canonical direct-sum map in the statement; the empty sum gives the zero-to-zero bijection.

theorem derivedGlobalSections_cohomology_coproduct (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)))
    let F := (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) 0 ⋙
      forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) AddCommGrpCat
    ∀ (I : Type u) (E : I → schemeDerivedQCohCategory X)
      (S : schemeDerivedCategory X) (ι : ∀ i, (E i).obj ⟶ S),
      IsColimit (Cofan.mk S ι) →
      Function.Bijective (DirectSum.toAddMonoid (fun i ↦ (F.map (ι i)).hom) :
        (⨁ i : I, F.obj (E i).obj) →+ F.obj S)
